records.content: Updated: 10:43 PM IST Monday, 20 Jul, 2026 PTI Amaravati : Andhra Pradesh Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav has said the Omicron RF.5 variant has been detected in the state following genome sequencing of four Covid-19 positive samples. The Health Department has sent four samples from Covid-19 cases reported in Kadapa district to a virology laboratory in Pune for testing, and the results have confirmed the presence of the RF.5 sub-lineage of the Omicron variant. "Genome sequencing at a virology laboratory in Pune has confirmed the presence of the Omicron RF.5 variant in four COVID-19 positive samples from Kadapa district," said Yadav in an official press release late on Saturday. The Minister held discussions with senior health officials over the phone regarding the findings from Pune and reviewed the prevailing Covid-19 situation in the southern state. RF.5 is a sub-lineage of the Omicron variant of the coronavirus and is among the several Omicron sub-lineages identified across the world, said the press release. Director of Medical Education Vishnuvardhan said the RF.5 variant was being monitored as part of routine genomic surveillance of SARS-CoV-2. The World Health Organisation (WHO) is also tracking the strain, which has been reported in higher numbers in Singapore and some countries in Southeast Asia. ADVERTISEMENT Citing scientific evidence currently available, he said there is no indication that RF.5 is more dangerous than other Omicron variants, and there was no need for the public to panic while only vigilance was required. RF.5 is a naturally evolved sub-lineage of the Omicron variant of SARS-CoV-2 and originated from the JN.1 variant through the LF.7 to PY.1.1.1 branches, the release said. The officials said that RF.5 is not a recombinant variant and is being continuously monitored by the WHO as part of routine genomic surveillance. The symptoms of RF.5 are similar to those seen in other Omicron sub-variants and include sore throat, cough, fever, headache, and body aches, said Vishnuvardhan. The Health Minister assured that Covid-19 cases in Andhra Pradesh continue to remain sporadic and hospitals have been fully prepared. He said special wards at teaching hospitals were being readied, while Covid testing kits and other necessary infrastructure were being arranged for detection of cases. According to the health department, so far, 16 Covid-19 cases have been reported in the State, including 12 cases reported up to July 16. PTI Bengaluru: Karnataka Minister U T Khader on Monday directed all districts to remain on high alert and step up surveillance and preparedness against viral fever and communicable diseases during the ongoing monsoon season. The state minister for Health and Family Welfare chaired a virtual review meeting to assess the preparedness of all districts. The meeting reviewed the current disease situation, surveillance activities, the availability of essential medicines, logistics, laboratory preparedness, human resources, vector control measures and public awareness initiatives. The State Surveillance Unit presented the latest update on Covid-19 and other communicable diseases, including influenza, Severe Acute Respiratory Infections, dengue, malaria, chikungunya, Japanese encephalitis and cholera, officials said. All 31 districts presented reports on their preparedness. According to the Health Department, the minister directed all districts to remain on high alert and ensure the uninterrupted availability of essential medicines, adequate hospital beds, trained manpower, laboratory support and emergency logistics at all government health facilities. ADVERTISEMENT He instructed District Health Officers to intensify disease surveillance under the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme, ensure timely reporting through the Integrated Health Information Platform, strengthen Rapid Response Teams, step up Information, Education and Communication activities, and promote preventive measures such as personal hygiene, safe drinking water, vector control and early healthcare-seeking behaviour. The minister stressed the need for house-to-house larval surveys, mosquito source reduction at construction sites and estates, and testing of all Influenza-Like Illness and Severe Acute Respiratory Infection cases. He also directed officials to coordinate closely with the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department, Urban Local Bodies, the Labour Department and other concerned departments, the statement said. He directed all districts to submit regular situation reports to the State Health Emergency Operations Centre. During the meeting, the State Surveillance Unit was activated at the HEOC to ensure continuous monitoring, rapid information sharing and a coordinated response to communicable disease outbreaks across the state, the statement added. PTI Bengaluru: A 38-year-old man was arrested for allegedly killing his father by assaulting him with an iron rod following a quarrel here, police said on Monday. The deceased was identified as Chandra Bahadur Shahi (58), a native of Kalikot district in Nepal, they said. The accused, Drona Bahadur Shahi, was arrested in connection with the incident, which occurred in the Varthur area on Sunday, police said. According to the police, Chandra had joined an apartment complex as a security guard on Friday. His son, Drona, arrived there on Sunday seeking a security job. ADVERTISEMENT At around 7 pm on Sunday, the two allegedly got into an argument, during which Drona is accused of assaulting his father with an iron rod, a senior police officer said. The injured man was initially taken to a private hospital by other workers and was later shifted to Victoria Hospital for further treatment. He succumbed to his injuries on Monday, police said. A case has been registered at the Varthur police station, and the accused has been arrested, they said. The body has been kept at Victoria Hospital for a post-mortem examination, police said, adding that further investigation is underway
